facts.value: Financial asset returns are assumed to be Gaussian in elementary models, yet empirical returns exhibit heavy tails, volatility clustering, and negative crash skewness.
Standard financial tools either oversimplify returns as normal (understating catastrophic downside risk) or present complex formulas without interactive visual intuition.
University students, data science learners, and quantitative finance researchers seeking a self-contained local experimental testbed.
Practical exploratory data analysis and educational quantitative laboratory; strictly not a novelty or research-gap project.
Implement dual return formulations (Simple and Logarithmic returns) with Indian market 252-day annualization convention.
Formulate downside tail risk analytics: Historical and Parametric Value at Risk (VaR 95%) and Expected Shortfall (CVaR).
Fit and compare parametric distributions (Normal vs Student-t MLE vs 2-component GMM) using AIC/BIC and Kolmogorov-Smirnov / Jarque-Bera tests.
Engineer sampling modules (seed-reproducible IID/Block Bootstrap) and walk-forward backtesting enforcing strict zero lookahead bias.
No live trade execution, no tick/orderbook streaming, no research-gap claims, and strictly no personalized financial advisory services.

Mandelbrot (1963) & Fama (1965): Leptokurtosis and heavy tails in asset returns. Artzner et al. (1999): Coherent risk measures & Expected Shortfall. Künsch (1989) / Politis & Romano (1994): Block bootstrap for dependent series.
López de Prado, M. (2018). Advances in Financial Machine Learning. Wiley. DOI: 10.1002/9781119482109. (Eliminates look-ahead leakage; enforces walk-forward backtesting).
